issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Rideable.messageOnRide(): the problem statement (UML and textual description) declares a no-argument method messageOnRide() returning a String and the template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments, but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements it in Pig and Seal with an int parameter. This changes the method signature (adds a required int parameter) and will cause compilation errors or confusion for students who implement the no-arg version as specified in the exercise text.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the messageOnRide method signature consistent across all artifacts. Options: (A) Align the solution with the problem statement: change Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) to messageOnRide() (no parameters) and update Pig and Seal implementations to return the no-arg string format "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"; update any solution tests accordingly. Or (B) If a speed parameter is intended, update the problem statement UML, the textual description, and the template Main (and any example calls) to specify messageOnRide(int speed) and show calls supplying a speed argument; update tests to call the method with an int. Prefer option (A) to match the existing UML and template usage unless the curriculum intends to teach parameterized ride messages.
